skill.name: ddd-tactical-patterns
skill.description: Apply Domain-Driven Design tactical patterns to code with entities, value objects, aggregates, repositories, and domain events.
skill.summary: Design behavior-rich domain models with clear invariants and aggregate boundaries.

content.value_statement: Many teams struggle to turn domain rules into maintainable code. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward aggregates, value objects, repositories, and domain events.
actual_capabilities: Identify invariants before designing aggregate boundaries.
Model immutable value objects with validation and value equality.
Place domain behavior inside entities and aggregates.
Define repository contracts around aggregate roots.
Use domain events for meaningful state transitions.
Review DDD designs with a tactical checklist.
limitations: It does not define strategic bounded contexts.
It does not choose databases, transports, or deployment architecture.
It does not replace tests for domain invariants.
It is not suited for simple CRUD features that do not need DDD.

use_cases.title: Refactor Anemic Models
use_cases.description: Move business rules from services or controllers into behavior-rich domain objects with explicit invariants.

use_cases.title: Design Aggregate Boundaries
use_cases.description: Choose aggregate roots and transaction boundaries before implementing write-side domain behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Domain Code
use_cases.description: Check repositories, value objects, and events against a concise tactical DDD checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Find Invariants
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for starting a DDD design from requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DDD tactical patterns skill to read these requirements and list the core invariants. Then suggest entities, value objects, and aggregate roots.

prompt_templates.title: Model an Aggregate
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for designing one aggregate boundary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DDD tactical patterns skill to design an aggregate for this workflow. Include the aggregate root, methods, invariants, repository boundary, and domain events.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Domain Logic
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for improving existing application code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DDD tactical patterns skill to refactor this anemic model. Move domain rules into entities or value objects and explain each changed responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Domain Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for reviewing a mature design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DDD tactical patterns skill to audit this domain model. Check aggregate boundaries, invariant enforcement, repository contracts, event payloads, and ORM leakage.

output_examples.input: A checkout workflow has orders, line items, payments, and inventory reservations.
output: The response identifies Order as an aggregate root and recommends enforcing submit and payment invariants inside it.
It suggests value objects for money, quantity, and order identifiers.
It recommends domain events such as OrderSubmitted with stable payloads.

output_examples.input: A service class validates account status before every transfer operation.
output: The response recommends moving transfer rules into the Account aggregate.
It separates account identifiers and money into value objects.
It defines a repository contract that loads and saves only aggregate roots.

output_examples.input: Review a repository that returns ORM records directly to domain services.
output: The response flags ORM leakage across the domain boundary.
It recommends mapping persistence records into domain objects.
It keeps query methods domain-friendly and tied to aggregate roots.

best_practices: Start with invariants and use them to choose aggregate boundaries.
Keep persistence concerns outside domain objects and repository contracts.
Use domain events for important state changes with minimal stable payloads.
anti_patterns: Do not apply full DDD complexity to simple CRUD workflows.
Do not place business rules only in controllers or application services.
Do not expose ORM entities as the domain model.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design code-level DDD models with aggregates, entities, value objects, repositories, and domain events.

faq.question: Does it define bounded contexts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on tactical patterns after strategic boundaries are already understood.

faq.question: Can it review existing code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can identify anemic models, weak invariants, repository leakage, and misplaced domain behavior.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready architecture?
faq.answer: No. It provides domain modeling guidance and should be combined with testing and architecture decisions.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it for pure UI work, API documentation, or simple CRUD tasks where tactical DDD adds unnecessary complexity.
